A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACT research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on PACIFIC, Abg-CoQA, and AmbigSQL, including benchmark results, component ablations, simulated conversations, and qualitative error analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, pseudo-labeled training results, and many-shot prompting experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds action-annotation agent G and an explicit action-inference step to Algorithm 1, enabling preference construction without gold action labels. The DPO objective and trajectory self-training remain intact. Its expanded explanation of replacing entire trajectories clarifies behavior already present in v1 Algorithm 2.

E1.justification: Both versions use PACIFIC, Abg-CoQA, and Spider-derived AmbigSQL for the same conversational tasks. AmbigSQL's construction, sizes, and ambiguity types remain unchanged. Pseudo-labeling and many-shot prompting reuse existing coverage under different experimental procedures.

E2.justification: v2 adds IRPO on PACIFIC and AmbigSQL, Gemini Pro SFT on PACIFIC, and Gemini Flash/Claude Sonnet/Claude Haiku prompting comparisons. Naive DPO becomes DPO-Dist, with its Ultra/Pro pairing replaced by Pro/Flash and Sonnet/Haiku variants. Gemini Ultra leaves the direct benchmark comparisons but remains in the clarification-need analysis. AmbigSQL also loses its Gemini Pro chain-of-thought comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot action pseudo-labeling, 50/100/250-example many-shot prompting, and Gemini SFT with four epochs and adapter size 4. v2 drops Accuracy and Weighted F1 reporting for PACIFIC/Abg-CoQA and adds Macro F1 for AmbigSQL. The stated Gemini Pro checkpoint changes from preview-0409 to 001; this does not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused analyses of dependence on gold action labels (Table 4) and sensitivity to the number of in-context conversations (Table A6). The original component and model-initialization ablations in Table 5, clarification-need analysis, and qualitative success/error cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new action-label agreement percentage is an additional point estimate, not a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerous comparator, pseudo-labeling, and many-shot results, including 98.5% agreement with PACIFIC action labels. In the retained 250-conversation Abg-CoQA SFT setting, Macro F1/turn similarity/trajectory similarity change from 45.1/61.0/59.8 to 53.5/64.0/66.2. Existing ACT benchmark scores and Table 5 values remain unchanged. Revised Gemini scores accompany a changed stated checkpoint and cannot establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The DPO loss, gradient, implicit reward formulation, and trajectory definitions remain unchanged. The added annotation step is procedural; v2 adds no theoretical guarantees, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion newly claim effective adaptation without gold dialogue-action labels, and the conclusion explicitly characterizes ACT as model agnostic. These extend the retained central contributions of sample-efficient ACT, AmbigSQL, and conversational evaluation.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly connects unreliable action evaluation to benchmark annotation agreement and argues for greater emphasis on multi-turn task completion. The sampling discussion shifts from off-policy negatives being too easy to distribution shift being difficult to overcome. The retained model-initialization ablation is reframed as evidence of model agnosticism.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code pointer, Gemini adapter-training details, updated Gemini model identifiers, and Claude access information. Hardware, most training hyperparameters, and detailed generation/classifier/simulator prompts are retained. The simulator explanation added to the main text largely summarizes existing appendix documentation.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds focused positioning against iterative DPO, self-play fine-tuning, IRPO, and Parrot, including an explicit priority claim for conversational-action contrastive learning. New references also support discussion of many-shot learning, WildFeedback, and test-time computation. The broader related-work framework remains intact.

P1.justification: The main text substantially rewrites and reorganizes the problem setup, evaluation, results, and ablation discussion. Simulator/classifier explanations move forward, Abg-CoQA results merge into Section 5.1, and qualitative examples and limitations consolidate in appendices. Terminology, author order, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document template and substantially restructures result tables, including metric columns and main-text/appendix placement. It adds the PACIFIC summary plot, trajectory-evaluation diagram, pseudo-label table, and many-shot table. The existing method diagram gains notation, while v1's qualitative Table 4 moves to Table A28.

improvement.justification: Pseudo-label experiments and IRPO comparisons provide useful evidence about practical applicability and competitiveness that v1 lacked; clearer trajectory-training prose and a code pointer also help. These gains are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: Table A6 broadly claims superiority over many-shot Gemini despite mixed results, and Table A8 still credits Gemini Ultra although its row was removed. The added controls improve the paper, but the expanded claims require more careful qualification.
